newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast crudes firm, but diffs idle on glut.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast crudes firm, but diffs idle on glut.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices added to Wednesday's gains early today, tracking West Texas Intermediate (WTI) as the bellwether crude got a boost from further reports of low crude stocks.

The U.S. government's Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed crude stocks fell by five million barrels for the week ended August 30, to hit 308 million. This came on the heels of lower stocks reported late Wednesday by the trade group American Petroleum Institute.
Deltas for Alaska North Slope, idle since August 22, remained at $2.05 a barrel under October cash WTI.
Traders said the discount would slip further because many refiners who normally buy were seen selling ANS in October.
"There's nothing out there that's gonna make it tighter in the near future," one trader said, noting autumn maintenance will back up more crude into the market.
Supplies of light and heavy crudes in PADD 5 West Coast storage have stayed abundant after a rash of summer shutdowns that left unprocessed crude in refineries.
And a mid-August power outage aggravated the problemed refineries, whose runs reportedly hit 88.8 percent of capacity last week, below the usual levels of 93 to 95, traders said.
One Northwest refinery offered crude at $2.10 off October WTI, while a Los Angeles refinery sold October ANS at prices based on the monthly average of September.
A major producer of ANS offered the grade at $2.00 under.
Values for Kern River stood at $16.40/16.60 cents a gallon while Wilmington remained $16.25/16.75 a barrel, after rising Wednesday with NYMEX-driven posted prices.
Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel, with little trading seen ahead of mid-September.
